items.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=(x+1)^{2}$ when $x<-1$, and by $f(x)=4-x$ when $x \ge -1$. Find $f(-4)$.
items.hint: Before you substitute anything, decide which of the two conditions the input $-4$ actually satisfies.
worked: Test the conditions: $-4<-1$ is true, so the first rule is the one that applies.
Substitute the input into that rule only: $f(-4)=(-4+1)^{2}=(-3)^{2}$.

items.stem: Which piecewise definition gives the same value as $f(x)=|x-3|$ for every real number $x$?
items.hint: The definition splits exactly where the inside expression $x-3$ changes sign, and on the side where the inside is negative you must take its opposite.
worked: The inside expression $x-3$ is zero at $x=3$, so that is where the definition splits.
When $x \ge 3$ the inside is not negative, so $|x-3|=x-3$.
When $x<3$ the inside is negative, so $|x-3|=-(x-3)=3-x$.
Check at $x=0$: the rule for $x<3$ gives $3-0=3$, and $|0-3|=3$.

items.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=(x+3)^{2}$ when $x<0$, and by $f(x)=2x+5$ when $x \ge 0$. Find every value of $x$ for which $f(x)=25$.
items.hint: Solve each rule separately, then keep a root only if it satisfies that rule's own condition.
worked: That rule is only in force when $x<0$, so $x=2$ is thrown out and $x=-8$ is kept.
Second rule: $2x+5=25$ gives $x=10$, and $10 \ge 0$, so $x=10$ is kept.
